epithet: The Event that sorts mankind in three
lede: When it comes there is no denying it: it brings some low and raises others high. All of humanity is divided that Day into three companies, and this surah goes through them one by one — then turns to the listener and asks him to explain his own existence.

names.name: al-Wāqiʿah
names.note: One of the names of the Resurrection, and the surah’s opening word: that which is bound to fall. The Prophet ﷺ named the surah by it when he listed those that had turned him grey (al-Tirmidhī 3297).

revelation.detail: Most hold it to be Makkan — Ibn al-Jawzī names Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, ʿAṭāʾ, ʿIkrimah, Qatādah, Jābir and Muqātil. One report from Ibn ʿAbbās, through ʿAṭiyyah, has it Madinan, and another excepts a single ayah (56:82) as Madinan. The traditional order places it forty-sixth.

evidence.quote: وَفِيها قَوْلانِ. أحَدُهُما: أنَّها مَكِّيَّةٌ، قالَهُ الأكْثَرُونَ، مِنهُمُ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ، والحَسَنُ، وعَطاءٌ، وعِكْرِمَةُ، وقَتادَةُ، وجابِرٌ، ومُقاتِلٌ
عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ قَالَ: قَالَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، قَدْ شبتَ؟ قَالَ: "شيَّبتني هُودٌ، وَالْوَاقِعَةُ، وَالْمُرْسَلَاتُ، وعَمَّ يَتَسَاءَلُونَ، وَإِذَا الشَّمْسُ كُوِّرَتْ

attested.quote: أخْرَجَ ابْنُ الضُّرَيْسِ، والنَّحّاسُ، وابْنُ مَرْدُويَهْ، والبَيْهَقِيُّ في «الدَّلائِلِ» عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ قالَ: نَزَلَتْ سُورَةُ «الواقِعَةِ» بِمَكَّةَ
attested.says: Ibn ʿAbbās: it came down in Makkah. Recorded by Ibn al-Ḍurays, al-Naḥḥās, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqī.

attested.quote: هي مَكِّيَّةٌ في قَوْلِ الحَسَنِ، وعِكْرِمَةَ، وجابِرٍ، وعَطاءٍ
attested.says: Makkan, in the saying of al-Ḥasan, ʿIkrimah, Jābir ibn Zayd and ʿAṭāʾ.

setting: No occasion is transmitted for the surah as a whole. Its place in the life of the Prophet ﷺ is told by a remark of Abū Bakr’s. He looked at him one day and said, “Messenger of Allah, you have gone grey.” He answered: “Hūd, al-Wāqiʿah, al-Mursalāt, ‘ʿAmma yatasāʾalūn’ and ‘Idhā l-shamsu kuwwirat’ have turned me grey.” This is one of the surahs whose weight he felt in his own body.

The people of Makkah thought in two classes: the noble and the rest. The surah replaces that with three, and they are not the classes anyone expected. The Foremost — those who raced to faith and to every good — are brought nearest. The People of the Right are saved. The People of the Left are lost. And of the Foremost it says: a throng from the earliest generations, and few from the later ones.

Then come four questions, each about something the listener does every day without thinking: the seed you emit, the crop you sow, the water you drink, the fire you kindle. Is it you who make it, or We? If We willed, We could make the crop chaff and the water bitter.

One passage near the end has an occasion that Ibn ʿAbbās relates in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim. Rain fell in the time of the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: “This morning some people are grateful and some are ungrateful. Some said: this is the mercy of Allah. Others said: such-and-such a star has proved true.” And the ayat came down — “I swear by the setting-places of the stars” — as far as: “and you make your share of it that you deny.”

occasions.title: Rain, and who is thanked for it
occasions.text: The people were given rain in the time of the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: “Some of the people have risen this morning grateful, and some of them ungrateful. They said: this is Allah’s mercy; and some of them said: such-and-such a rain-star has been true.” Then this was revealed: “I swear by the setting-places of the stars…” until “and you make your provision that you deny.”

aim: To strike fear of the Day of Resurrection, establish that it will occur, set out the kinds of people on it, and make plain the recompense of each.
themes: The Foremost, the Right and the Left

outline.title: When it falls
outline.summary: When the Event occurs — and none can deny its occurring — bringing low and raising high; when the earth is shaken and the mountains crumbled to scattered dust; you will be three kinds: the People of the Right, the People of the Left, and the Foremost, the foremost.

outline.title: The Foremost
outline.summary: They are those brought near, in Gardens of Delight: many from the first generations and few from the later. On thrones inlaid, facing one another; served by youths who do not age, with cups from a flowing spring that brings no headache; whatever fruit they choose and the meat of fowl they desire; and companions like hidden pearls — a reward for what they used to do. They hear no idle or sinful talk there, only: “Peace, peace.”

outline.title: The People of the Right
outline.summary: Among thornless lote-trees and clustered banana-trees, shade extended and water ever-flowing, fruit in abundance, never cut off and never forbidden, and couches raised high. A throng from the first generations, and a throng from the later.

outline.title: The People of the Left
outline.summary: In scorching wind and scalding water, and a shade of black smoke, neither cool nor kind. They lived before that in luxury, persisted in the great sin, and used to say: “When we are dead, and dust and bones, shall we really be raised?” Say: the first and the last will be gathered. Then you will eat of the tree of Zaqqūm and drink boiling water on top of it, as thirst-maddened camels drink. That is their welcome on the Day of Recompense.

outline.title: Four questions
outline.summary: We created you; why then will you not believe? Have you considered the seed you emit — do you create it, or do We? The seed you sow — do you make it grow? The water you drink — did you bring it down from the cloud? The fire you kindle — did you make its tree? So glorify the name of your Lord, the Tremendous.

outline.title: A noble Qurʾan
outline.summary: I swear by the setting-places of the stars — and it is a mighty oath, if only you knew: this is a noble Qurʾan, in a Book well guarded, which none touch but the purified; a sending down from the Lord of the worlds. Is it this discourse that you make light of, and make your thanks that you deny?

outline.title: At the throat
outline.summary: Why, then, when the soul reaches the throat, and you are there looking on — and We are nearer to him than you, though you do not see — why do you not bring it back, if you are not to be held to account? If he is of those brought near: rest, and fragrance, and a Garden of Delight. If of the People of the Right: “Peace to you.” If of the deniers gone astray: a welcome of boiling water, and burning in Hell. This is the certain truth. So glorify the name of your Lord, the Tremendous.

keyAyah.why: The Foremost, named twice. They are the measure the surah holds up: not those who were merely saved, but those who raced.

virtues.text: Abū Bakr said: “Messenger of Allah, you have gone grey.” He ﷺ said: “Hūd, al-Wāqiʿah, al-Mursalāt, ‘ʿAmma yatasāʾalūn’ and ‘Idhā l-shamsu kuwwirat’ have turned me grey.”
virtues.arabic: شَيَّبَتْنِي هُودٌ وَالْوَاقِعَةُ وَالْمُرْسَلاَتُ وَعَمَّ يَتَسَاءَلُونَ وَإِذَا الشَّمْسُ كُوِّرَتْ

before: Al-Raḥmān described two pairs of gardens, one above the other. Al-Wāqiʿah says for whom: the higher for the Foremost, the other for the People of the Right — and adds the third company, which al-Raḥmān had called the guilty.
after: Al-Wāqiʿah ends: glorify the name of your Lord, the Tremendous. Al-Ḥadīd begins: everything in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah.
